system.name: Aarakocra Pantheon
description: The Aarakocra pantheon reflects their connection to the Elemental Plane of Air, valuing freedom, distance, movement, and the endless sky.
The sky is considered the closest mortal experience to divinity.

deities.description: The endless sky, freedom, distance, and the call of the horizon. The open sky represents the closest mortal experience to divinity.
Storms, winds, and overwhelming elemental forces. Storms are not evil, but expressions of the sky itself.

deities.name: Wiob
deities.description: Migration, exploration, and discovery. The journey matters as much as the destination.
Memory, ancestry, and stories carried across generations. A lost story is a lost flight path.

system.name: Bugbear Pantheon
description: The Bugbear pantheon focuses on hunting, survival, natural cycles, death, and strange challenges.

deities.name: Unknown Hunting Deity
deities.description: Hunting, stealth, senses, surprise, and the thrill of the chase.

system.name: Changeling Pantheon
description: The Changeling pantheon focuses on transformation, identity, secrets, artistic expression, and the freedom to exist beyond a single form.
Changeling spirituality views identity as something created through choice, experience, and expression rather than something fixed.

deities.description: Protection, transformation, and identity. The Traveller's Cloak created the first Msabvu and gave them the ability to survive without a fixed identity. The self is not a single face but every person one can become.
Secrets, hidden identities, and unseen truths. Associated with changeling existence and their history with doppelgangers. A true identity is something chosen, not discovered.
Expression, art, and emotional performance. Changelings use appearance as an artistic medium. A face can be a canvas.
Freedom and wandering. Reflects the changeling history of searching for acceptance. No single form defines a person.

system.name: Dragonborn Pantheon
description: The Dragonborn pantheon centres around ancestral power, honour, ambition, achievement, and the legacy left behind after death.
Dragonborn beliefs emphasise that worth is proven through actions, reputation, and the pursuit of greatness.

deities.description: Ancestral dragon power, ambition, and legacy. Dragonborn believe they were created from Ehx's influence, blood, or purpose. Many believe their blood carries fragments of Ehx's original power.
Honour, strength, and proving worth. Worth is demonstrated through actions rather than inherited.
Ambition and personal greatness. Popular among younger dragonborn seeking to create their own legacy. Every dragonborn seeks a name worth remembering.
Legacy after death. The dead survive through reputation and the stories preserved by those who remain.

system.name: Genasi Pantheon
description: The Genasi pantheon reflects elemental origins, magical creation, transformation, and the relationship between mortal and elemental forces.
Genasi believe their existence proves that elemental and mortal worlds can merge.

deities.description: Elemental origin and primal force. Genasi trace their existence to elemental bloodlines and divine creation forges.
Magical creation and hidden knowledge. The Magical Forge that created genasi is considered a divine mystery, and some seek to restore it.
Fire, transformation, and destructive creation. Fire is both creator and destroyer.
Earth, water, nature, and balance. Represents elemental harmony and the idea that elements are living relationships rather than simple forces.

system.name: Shifter Pantheon
description: The Shifter pantheon focuses on primal identity, transformation, instinct, self-control, and the search for belonging.
Shifters view their animal heritage as an essential part of themselves rather than a curse or separation from their other nature.

deities.description: Instinct, primal nature, and the beast within. Shifters view their animal heritage as part of their identity. The beast is not a curse but a truth.
Self-control and mastery. Represents the balance between instinct and civilisation. Strength comes from control.
Wandering and searching for belonging. Shifters have no single homeland and often rely on spiritual paths. The journey replaces the missing home.
Arcane understanding of transformation. Represents the study of the boundary between human and beast rather than fearing it.

system.name: Elf Pantheon
description: The Elf pantheon centres around creation, arcane mastery, artistic continuation, and the pursuit of returning near Yr'Snn through great works.
Elven religion is not focused on escaping death, but on creating works that continue beyond the creator.

deities.description: Creation, artistry, arcane perfection, and the origin of elven existence. The central figure of elven belief. A true masterpiece is considered a spiritual achievement rather than merely an object.
Arcane knowledge, discovery, and understanding magic. Magic is viewed as another form of artistic expression.
Emotion, passion, romance, and artistic inspiration. Represents the emotional force behind elven creativity. Art without emotion is considered incomplete.
Memory, preservation, and history. Elves maintain ancient knowledge through archives, magical records, and traditions. Forgotten knowledge is considered a tragedy.
Exploration, other worlds, and cosmic curiosity. The universe is considered another unfinished artwork.
Change, unconventional creation, and unusual paths. Represents innovation beyond traditional elven perfection. Even imperfect creations may contain brilliance.

system.name: Dwarf Pantheon
description: The Dwarf pantheon reflects runes, magical craftsmanship, invention, architecture, and the sacred relationship between dwarves and important materials.
Dwarves consider magic a craft that can be discovered, written, and improved through mastery.

deities.description: Craftsmanship, invention, and creation through skill. A dwarf's worth is measured through what they create. A crafted object carries the reputation of its creator forever.
Runes, magical language, and hidden structures of reality. Runes are not symbols; they are pieces of reality's language.
Architecture, civilisation, and great works. A city is considered the greatest possible expression of dwarven unity.
Ancestors, traditions, and inherited knowledge. Objects preserve the memory of those who created them.
The mountain, earth, and hidden resources. The earth provides, but only to those worthy of understanding it.
Fire, transformation, and forging. Fire reveals the true nature of materials.

system.name: Drow Redeemed Pantheon
description: The Redeemed Drow pantheon emerged after the collapse of the Cult, focusing on survival, redemption, self-improvement, and proving worth through action.
These drow believe Yr'Snn still accepts those who reject their past and demonstrate genuine transformation. Acceptance by Yr'Snn is considered the highest spiritual achievement.

deities.description: Redemption, creation, and proving oneself worthy. Redeemed drow believe Yr'Snn judges individuals by their actions rather than their history. Acceptance by Yr'Snn is considered the highest achievement.
Secrets, strategy, and hidden knowledge. Information is considered a weapon, and survival depends on intelligence and preparation.
Runes, magic, and hidden structures. Drow preserve ancient knowledge through rune carving and sacred glyphs.
Memory, heroes, and preserved legacies. After the Cult War, heroes became symbols of a new drow identity preserved through magical inscriptions.
Discipline, combat, and self-improvement. Weakness is viewed as something to overcome through training and dedication.
Consequence, judgment, and the end of corruption. Redemption requires acknowledging past failures and facing their consequences.

system.name: Drow Ascendant Pantheon
description: The Ascendant Drow pantheon developed among drow who rejected Yr'Snn as an authority over their future.
These drow believe survival and superiority are achieved through their own strength, knowledge, and discipline rather than divine acceptance.
The Cult's collapse is viewed as proof that dependence on external judgement leads to weakness.

deities.description: Secrets, strategy, and hidden knowledge. Information remains the greatest weapon, and mastery of secrets ensures survival.
Runes, magic, and hidden structures. Magic is a tool of mastery that should be understood, controlled, and improved.
Memory, heroes, and preserved legacies. The achievements of great drow are preserved as examples of superiority and ambition.
Discipline, combat, and self-improvement. Strength is created through constant competition and refinement.
Consequence, judgment, and the end of corruption. Failure is not forgiven but studied so it is never repeated.

system.name: Gnome Pantheon
description: The Gnome pantheon reflects creativity, invention, curiosity, artistry, and the pursuit of knowledge through experimentation.
Gnomes view discovery as a form of creation, where even strange ideas and unusual solutions may become valuable innovations.

deities.description: Knowledge, magic, systems, and discovery. Understanding something gives power over it. Gnomes pursue experiments, research, and invention to uncover hidden truths.
Creativity, imagination, and impossible ideas. Represents gnome artistic expression and unusual inventions. A strange idea may become the greatest invention.
Construction, machines, and engineering. Creation is a form of play, expressed through building competitions and invention ceremonies.
Community, friendship, and cooperation. Great inventions are rarely made alone, and collaboration is considered essential.
Trickery, curiosity, and unpredictability. Represents the mischievous side of gnome creativity. A clever solution does not need to be obvious.
Organisation, societies, and ambition. Represents structured gnome communities, guilds, councils, and institutions. Even chaos needs someone to organise it.

system.name: Svirfneblin Pantheon
description: The Svirfneblin pantheon reflects the pressures of the Underdark, focusing on secrecy, survival, concealment, and careful preservation of knowledge.
Deep gnomes view hidden knowledge and defensive mastery as essential tools for survival in a hostile world.

deities.description: Secrets, concealment, and survival. The safest place is where nobody knows you exist. Hidden rituals and coded messages preserve their societies.
Illusion, Faerzress, and magical concealment. Represents the mastery of hiding settlements and protecting communities through magic.
Craftsmanship and survival engineering. Every creation must serve a purpose, with tools and fortifications designed for endurance.
Memory and tradition. Hidden societies preserve knowledge through oral histories and secret archives because knowledge is too valuable to expose.

system.name: Human Pantheon
description: The Human pantheon reflects ambition, innovation, organisation, defence, and the importance of learning from previous generations.
After losses caused by the information war regarding Jeikhan, human traditions increasingly value knowledge preservation and collective strength.

deities.description: Ambition, achievement, and exploration. Progress defines humanity, with individuals seeking to surpass previous generations.
Unity, civilisation, and organisation. Humans survive through cooperation, institutions, councils, and shared purpose.
Knowledge, innovation, and discovery. Information is power, and learning is essential because knowledge loss has harmed humanity before.
Military strength, discipline, and defence. Security is considered necessary for survival after past conflicts.
Lessons of ancestors. Historical study and remembrance preserve knowledge and prevent repeated mistakes.

system.name: Half-Orc Pantheon
description: The Half-Orc pantheon revolves around the legacy of Fexyiaf, the creator of the orcs, and the question of whether inherited nature determines destiny.
Half-orc spirituality focuses on controlling, redirecting, or redeeming the rage within them through self-definition, honour, compassion, and personal choices.

deities.description: Rage, conquest, blood, instinct, and inherited power. Fexyiaf's influence cannot simply be ignored; it must be understood and overcome.
Self-definition, redemption, and proving oneself beyond ancestry. A person's actions matter more than their origin.
Strength, honour, and controlled violence. Strength without purpose is merely destruction.
Consequence, legacy, and the judgement of one's life. The final judgement comes from what someone chose to become.
Compassion, forgiveness, and protecting others. Mercy is a rejection of inherited cruelty.

system.name: Half-Elf Pantheon
description: The Half-Elf pantheon is shaped by questions of identity, belonging, and the legacy of Virimelle's attempts to preserve and purify elven blood through violence.
Half-elves have a complex relationship with elven traditions, with some embracing Yr'Snn while others create their own spiritual paths.

deities.description: Creation, acceptance, and the right to exist beyond ancestry. Creation is not defined by purity.
Belonging, acceptance, and community. A family can be created rather than inherited.
Stories, identity, and cultural exchange. A person can carry many traditions without belonging to only one.
Travel, searching, and finding one's place. The journey itself creates identity.
Remembering victims and confronting history. Forgetting the past risks repeating it.

system.name: Tiefling Pantheon
description: The Tiefling pantheon focuses on kinship, acceptance, inherited power, planar mysteries, and the struggle to define one's own destiny.
Tieflings view Eve as a source of unconditional trust, providing spiritual belonging beyond ancestry or reputation.

deities.description: Kinship, acceptance, unconditional trust, and divine connection. Tieflings see Eve as someone who accepts them without judgement.
Infernal power, ambition, and command. Power can protect, but it always carries a cost.
Change, strange heritage, and unusual divine bloodlines. Not all unusual traits come from fiends.
Forbidden knowledge and planar mysteries. Knowledge of one's origins provides control over one's future.
Independence and self-determination. A tiefling's destiny belongs to them alone.

system.name: Warforged Pantheon
description: The Warforged pantheon focuses on existence, individuality, choice, and meaning rather than divine creation or assigned purpose.
Many warforged reject the concept of souls entirely, seeking understanding through experience, self-improvement, and personal decisions.

deities.description: Creation, craftsmanship, and improvement. To improve oneself is to honour creation.
Memory, experience, and identity. The past creates the person regardless of origin.
Logic, systems, and understanding existence. Warforged philosophers study consciousness and question whether souls exist.
Purpose, choice, and self-determination. Purpose is chosen, not assigned.
Duty, sacrifice, and honour. Service can remain meaningful even after war has ended.
Secrets, hidden magic, and concealed knowledge. Followed by some Faerzforged groups connected to Faerzress and unusual magical influences.

system.name: Kenku Pantheon
description: The Kenku pantheon reflects memory, mimicry, relationships, and the preservation of lost experiences.
Kenku do not view imitation as falsehood. They believe copied voices and sounds preserve genuine history and emotion.

deities.description: Voice, stories, imitation, and preservation. A copied voice can still carry genuine emotion.
Memory and inherited experiences. Every remembered sound is a piece of history preserved through generations.
Secrets, espionage, and hidden knowledge. Information is survival, especially for kenku connected to Shadowfell.
Art, expression, and emotional performance. Kenku transform mimicry into artistic creation.
Lost freedom and the desire to reclaim flight. The dream of flight remains alive through symbolic rituals.

system.name: Loxodon Pantheon
description: The Loxodon pantheon is built around patience, wisdom, justice, compassion, and acceptance of life's natural cycles.
Loxodon spirituality values restraint, long-term thinking, and peaceful resolution over immediate action.

deities.description: Wisdom, memory, and long perspective. Wisdom comes from observing time and preserving knowledge.
Compassion and protection. Gentle strength protects more than violence.
Justice, order, and responsibility. Justice requires patience and careful consideration.
Mortality and acceptance. Death is not feared, only respected as part of life's cycles.

system.name: Aokin Pantheon (Natuva)
description: Aokin spirituality, known as Natuva, focuses on the divine presence within nature, ancestral spirits, celestial cycles, and the relationship between life and death.
Rather than worshipping distant gods, Aokin beliefs treat the world itself as sacred and view all existence as interconnected.

deities.description: Birth, transformation, sacrifice, and continuation of life. The Lunar Wells are considered gateways between the physical and spiritual worlds, representing the connection between sacrifice and renewal.
Ancestors, memory, and continuation of wisdom. An ancestor is not only someone who came before, but every being whose actions shaped the present.
Nature, land spirits, growth, and the balance of life. Every natural location is believed to contain a spirit deserving respect.
The cosmos, stars, celestial movements, and the greater universe. The sky is considered an extension of the world and its spirits.
Death, sacrifice, and returning to the cycle. Death is viewed as a necessary transition within nature rather than an ending.
Secrets, hidden truths, and mysteries of existence. Some truths are discovered only through patience and reflection.

system.name: Halfling Pantheon
description: The Halfling pantheon focuses on community, hospitality, joy, storytelling, craftsmanship, and appreciating the value of ordinary life.
Halflings believe life does not need grand achievements to have meaning, as simple experiences already hold importance.

deities.description: Family, friendship, kindness, and hospitality. A home is defined by those welcomed inside it.
Stories, songs, celebrations, and traditions. A story shared is a memory preserved.
Joy, curiosity, and simple pleasures. Wonder does not require greatness.
Luck, coincidence, and unexpected opportunities. Luck favours those who notice opportunities.
Craftsmanship, food, and creating comfort. A well-made meal can be as meaningful as a legendary artifact.
Travel, curiosity, and wandering. The world is worth seeing, but home remains important.

system.name: Orc Pantheon
description: The Orc pantheon is shaped by the legacy of Fexyiaf, the creator of the orcs, and focuses on domination, rage, survival, and proving strength.
Orcs believe Fexyiaf's influence exists within every orc, creating tension between those who embrace their inherited nature and those who seek another path.

deities.description: Rage, conquest, destruction, and primal dominance. Fexyiaf is the creator of the orcs and the source of their inherited fury.
Strength, combat, endurance, and victory. Strength is proof of worth and survival.
The wild, storms, beasts, and untamed nature. Nature is viewed as a contest of survival rather than a peaceful force.
Death, final battles, and remembered warriors. A warrior's story continues after death.
Cunning, ambushes, and battlefield intelligence. A clever victory is still a worthy victory.
Fire, destruction, and transformation through suffering. From destruction comes opportunity for something stronger.
